title: A border meets the fill and the edge cleanly, with nothing showing through
goal: Put an inner border on a rectangle and a hairline of the fill colour still shows along the outside of it. The same thing happens on an outside border, where a hairline shows along the inside of it, between the border and the fill. A border should meet what is on either side of it cleanly: no seam of the fill, and no seam of the background, at any zoom.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-09 with a magnified screenshot: a red fill showing faintly along the outer edge of a black inner border. Where to look, from a read of Sources/PhotonzRender/DocumentRenderer.swift: the ring is built in ringed at line 988 as an outer rounded rectangle with an inner one punched out of it (the flat path around lines 1011 to 1023), then composited OVER the layer image. So the fill is still painted underneath, and the ring only covers it as well as its own antialiased edge allows; two antialiased edges meeting at the same boundary do not sum to full coverage, which is exactly the hairline seen. Two candidate fixes to weigh and record: draw the ring so its outer edge is the shape's own outer edge and the fill is clipped to the ring's inner edge rather than painted to the boundary, or composite the ring with the fill already cut back. The first is likely right because it keeps one antialiased outer edge for the whole shape rather than two stacked. Note the generator used is CIFilter.roundedRectangleGenerator (line 1323), so whatever is chosen has to work with that rather than assume a path stroke.

UPDATED 2026-09-09 by the user, with a second magnified screenshot (green background, black outside border, red fill): “i complained earlier about fill color bleeding through the outside of an inner border. This also applies to the inside of an outer border.” So this is one bug with two faces, not two bugs. Wherever the ring is composited OVER what is already painted, the ring’s antialiased edge and the edge underneath it do not sum to full coverage, and a hairline of whatever is underneath shows through: the FILL on the outer edge of an inner border, the BACKGROUND on the inner edge of an outside border. Fix it once at the compositing level rather than nudging geometry per position, and verify all three positions (inside, centred, outside) in the same pass.
acceptance: Reproduce BOTH first and record the numbers in the log: sample the pixels across the edge of a filled rectangle with an inner border, and across the inner edge of one with an outside border, and say how wide each leaking band is and what colour it is
With an inner border, no pixel outside the border’s inner edge carries any of the fill colour, checked by sampling rather than by eye, at one hundred percent and at several zooms
With an outside border, no pixel between the border and the fill carries any of the background colour, checked the same way
The outside of the shape stays properly antialiased against the background, so removing the leaks does not leave a hard jagged edge
A shape with a rounded corner behaves the same all the way round the corner, where the curves are closest together
A centred border gets the same check on both of its edges, so the fix does not trade one seam for another
Pixel tests in PhotonzRender cover the inner-border outer edge and the outside-border inner edge, written before the change
Audit written under queue/audits/ with magnified corners and edges before and after for all three border positions, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: user extended: same seam on the inside of an outside border

REPRODUCED first, with numbers. Red rounded rect (radius 20) on a green sheet, black border 8 wide, samples across the corner arc at row y=53: INNER border, outer edge -- x=68 r=81 g=193, x=69 r=63 g=21, so up to 32% of the FILL bleeding through what should be a pure background-to-border transition, two pixels wide. OUTSIDE border, inner edge -- x=68 r=64 g=157, x=69 r=234 g=97, so up to 62% of the BACKGROUND showing between the border and the fill, two pixels wide. A straight edge on whole pixels leaks nothing: the seam is purely a conflation artifact wherever an edge is antialiased.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW before building. The obvious fix (nudge the ring's geometry half a pixel so it overlaps its neighbours) was rejected: it hides the seam by making the border render half a pixel thicker than it measures, and this is a redlining tool where a border's stated width is the point. The 'draw the concentric bands solid, outside in' fix was rejected too: it fills the GAP of a ring standing off its edge with the ring's colour, and it paints over what a see-through ring is meant to show. Both would have traded the user's bug for a quieter one.

FIX, at the compositing level as the task asked, in two halves. (1) DocumentRenderer.laid: a ring is no longer composited OVER the picture, it SHARES the pixel with it by area. The picture underneath is taken to fill the pixel from the inside out, which is true of every shape a ring hugs, so its share of the band is min(max(0, a - inner), outer - inner) and it is held back by that fraction of itself. Ring and picture are then ADDED, since they do not overlap. The ring's own paint alpha scales the hold-back, so a half transparent border still shows the fill under it. (2) DocumentRenderer.roundedRectMask: the ring's silhouettes are now DRAWN through Core Graphics instead of generated by CIRoundedRectangleGenerator. Sharing a pixel by area only works if both sides measure the same edge, and the generator disagrees with the shape rasterizer by up to 9/255 on the same 20 point corner -- enough to leave a residual hairline. A Core Graphics fill of the same path matches the shape byte for byte (measured).

One subtle trap worth recording: the coverage greys inside laid MUST NOT be cropped to the picture's extent. A cropped grey is see-through past its edge, and CISubtractBlendMode / CIDarkenBlendMode / CIDivideBlendMode then have two half-there operands to reconcile instead of two numbers to subtract. That alone left a seam on every layer whose frame lands between two pixels (2.75x zoom), and looked exactly like a geometry bug.

VERIFIED. New Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/BorderSeamRenderTests.swift, written before the change, asserts the invariant a person actually sees: no single pixel may carry some of the fill AND some of the background, since the border separates them. Covers all three positions on a rounded corner, square corners, thin rings, ovals, four zooms (1.5x, 2x, 2.75x, 4x), a ring standing off the edge, and a half transparent ring. All zero leaks except an oval's OUTSIDE border, which keeps 20 pixels at under 70/255 (was hundreds at three times that) because an oval's ring is a stroke whose inner boundary is genuinely not the oval; filed as an-oval-s-outside-border-meets-the-oval-cleanly. Full suite 5485 tests green. Border playtest walks: 6 passed, 0 failed.

PERF NOTE (composite path). 12MP/10-layer interactive edit 5.5ms -> 6.4ms, full render 38.2ms -> 36.9ms, crisp tile at 400% 9.8ms -> 10.5ms, export at 2x 96ms -> 118ms, and the heaviest case, an interactive edit inside a styled group of five, 35.8ms -> 45.9ms. All inside their budgets. The first cut was far worse (12.8ms interactive) because a 12 megapixel silhouette was being baked every frame; masks are now only drawn when they fit the cache (2 megapixels) and the cache is held to an 8 megapixel budget, with anything bigger falling back to the generator. Confining the correction to the band itself is filed as drawing-a-border-costs-only-the-band-it-covers.
Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-border-seam.json, with a ten times magnified before and after of all three positions round a corner, and a real screen capture from the probe.

Rings are now laid on the picture and share each pixel by area (DocumentRenderer.laid), and their silhouettes are drawn through Core Graphics so they measure the same edge the shape does (roundedRectMask). Inner, centred and outside borders all leak nothing at 1x and at 1.5x/2x/2.75x/4x, on round and square corners, verified by pixel sampling in the new BorderSeamRenderTests; full suite 5485 green, six border playtest walks pass. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-09-border-seam.json with 10x magnified before/after. Two follow-ups filed: the oval outside border residual, and confining the cost to the band.
